questions.stem: Which of the following is the Antidote for belladonna poisoning?
questions.solutionHtml:
Physostigmine

Belladonna poisoning is due to the consumption of plant Atropa Belladonna plant. Its active constituent is mainly atropine and other anticholinergic substances. Physostigmine is an indirectly acting parasympathomimetic drug that acts by increasing Acetylcholine by blocking the Acetylcholinesterase enzyme. Thus it reverses the action of the muscarinic receptor blockade by atropine in belladonna poisoning.

  • Physostigmine- 0.5–2 mg i.v.
  • Repeated as required is the specific antidote for poisoning with belladonna or other anticholinergics
  • It penetrates the blood-brain barrier and antagonizes both central and peripheral actions
  • Neostigmine and pyridostigmine don’t cross BBB
  • Atropine is also called belladonna


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 122

questions.stem: A patient presented in the emergency with tachycardia, hyperthermia, bronchial dilatation, and constipation. The person is likely to be suffering from an overdose of:
questions.solutionHtml:
Atropine
  • These are the characteristic features of anticholinergic overdose.
  • Anticholinergics inhibit cholinergic responses and produce a state that can be remembered by the mnemonics given below.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 126

Inhibition of acetylcholine release
  • Two toxins interfere with cholinergic transmission by affecting release: botulinum toxin inhibits release, while black widow spider toxin induces massive release and depletion
  • Hemicholinium blocks choline uptake, which is the rate-limiting step in ACh synthesis


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 110

questions.stem: Botulinum toxin is used in the following conditions except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Atonic bladder
  • Botulinum toxin acts by inhibiting the Ach release from the vesicles thus having antimuscarinic action. In the atonic bladder, there is already decreased muscarinic action and we need to stimulate that. Thus, botox can’t be given here.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 110
